basic_identification.full_title: Treatment and Disposal of Effluents of Petroleum Refining Industry — Guidelines (First Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Environment Pollution / Environmental Protection and Waste Management (approved by the newly formed Environment and Ecology Division Council and finalized by the Environment Pollution Sectional Committee, EED 02, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard provides guidelines and design considerations for the methods of treatment and disposal of effluents originating from petroleum refineries. It establishes characteristics of composite waste water and recommends practical biological, chemical, and physical treatment technologies to comply with Minimal National Standards (MINAS).

version_status_and_amendments.edition_year_of_copy: First Revision, April 2025 (established to reflect changes in refinery configurations and updated wastewater characteristics over the last 40 years)
version_status_and_amendments.amendment_slips: No active amendments have been issued on this newly established 2025 revision (NIL on this copy).

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Procedural Guidelines / Code of Practice (Environmental Protection / Industrial Waste Management)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Procedural and Guidelines Standard. Compliance with IS 10044:2025 is verified through state pollution control boards, environmental impact assessments (EIA), and safety audits. While there is no direct BIS 'ISI Mark' stamp for IS 10044 itself, compliance with its wastewater treatment schemes, oil limits, and explosion-proof drainage designs is universally mandated in public refinery design, engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contracts across India.

requirements.detail: All waste streams subject to accidental or continuous oil contamination must be routed through gravity separators or surge ponds to facilitate effective physical oil removal.

Dissolved Air Flotation (DAF) must be applied as a primary treatment step to inject micron-sized air bubbles that float fat, oil, grease (O&G), and low-density chemically coagulated suspended solids to the surface for skimming. This reduces residual oil after gravity separation but is not meant for oil recovery.

Hydrodynamic cavitation may be utilized as a high-intensity physical pre-treatment step. Water flows through a high-velocity physical constriction, creating vapor-filled cavities (cavitation bubbles) that collapse with intense localized forces (shockwaves, micro-jets) to disrupt chemical bonds, break down large organic molecules, and make them highly amenable to subsequent biological treatment.

requirements.requirement_type: Explosion-Proof Collection and Drainage System Safety
requirements.detail: Collecting system designs must prioritize fire and explosion prevention above standard sanitary sewage criteria. All branch or lateral sewers must be isolated from main sewers using liquid water seals and water-sealed manholes to prevent the travel of explosive hydrocarbon vapours. Properly designed vents must be high enough to disperse volatile vapours safely and prevent their accumulation at ground elevation.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 10044 : 2025 (First Revision) is the national Indian Standard code of practice specifying guidelines for the treatment, management, and safe disposal of effluents originating from the petroleum refining industry. Formulated under the Environment Pollution Sectional Committee, this revision updates the wastewater characteristics and treatment guidelines to reflect modern refining units. It defines strict segregation for five classes of wastewater, establishes performance thresholds for biological treatment (such as oil tolerances of 100 ppm for trickling filters and 25 ppm for activated sludge systems), and outlines advanced chemical neutralization, dissolved air flotation, and hydrodynamic cavitation methods. Crucially, the standard enforces strict explosion-proof collection designs—mandating water-sealed isolation manholes and high-elevation vents—to prevent fire and vapor-propagation hazards across refinery drainage systems.
